decisions.statement: A command's page names the export the command runs.
What one command run cost is appended beside the page of the command that ran.
The cost is taken around the whole call rather than around any part of it.
A call reaching no command is recorded nowhere.
A line appended here takes no turn over any file another writer has.
A command is found through the page type reached by its id rather than by a spelled slug.
The file with a command's code is answered from the page the index names.
No call here refreshes the index, whatever the index is missing.
A call naming no command where the index is unusable names the call that builds one.
The call that refreshes the index is answered where the index is unusable.
The code that refreshes the index is imported rather than named by a path.
Each leading word of the command line steps one level down the command tree.
A word reaches a level only where that level's own page states that word as its name.
The descent starts at the parts the page type saying what a command is states.
Each level after that is looked for among the parts the level above it states.
A word that could be no part of a slug ends the walk before that word.
The level the words reach is the command called where that level is a command.
A level that is a namespace is stepped through where a word reaches below it.
The words past the level a command sits at are the arguments the command is handed.
How deep the walk goes is bounded by the words the line offers rather than by a count.
Naming a command costs one read of what the index carries for every command and namespace.
A name carried by more than one command is refused rather than chosen between.
A name carried by more than one namespace is refused rather than chosen between.
Such a refusal names the word the call wrote rather than the slug of any page.
Such a refusal is the same whatever order the pages it names were written in.
A command is told the call as that call was written on the command line.
That call is told whole as one line as well as word by word.
A word carrying a space is written back inside single quotes.
A command filing a record of its run writes that line rather than spelling one.
A help answer is titled by the call that reached the command.
A help answer carries the directives the command's own page states.
It carries the directives every namespace above that command states.
A namespace above is a level the descent stepped through to reach the command.
The namespaces are read widest first, and the command's own come last.
No page is loaded again to read what a namespace above states.
No directive a page type states reaches a help answer.
The argument pages a command names are read here and handed to the help answer.
An argument name reaching no one page is written into no help answer.
The decision kinds that do not hold yet are the kinds naming the intent group.
Which kinds those are is read from beside the page rather than spelled here.
A namespace listing is titled by the call that reached the namespace.
A name no command and no namespace carries is answered with the commands there are.
A name the caller got wrong is refused as a fault of the call.
A fault in the index or in a command's own page is refused as a fault of the data.
Such a name near a command's or a namespace's is refused with that name pointed at.
A name a namespace has rather than a command is answered with what that namespace holds.
The deepest namespace the words reach is the namespace answered with.
A word past that namespace, reaching nothing that namespace holds, is refused.
The words after that one are named in the refusal with it.
Such a refusal names the call reaching that namespace and everything that namespace holds.
A word near a name that namespace holds is refused with that name pointed at.
Two names equally near a word are told apart by name order rather than by the order written.
The help flag past a namespace asks for that namespace's listing.
One descent reaches both, so a namespace is looked for in no second descent.
A part is listed by the name that part's own page states.
A part stating no name is listed by its slug.
A part is listed with the definition that part's own page states.
A part that is no command and no namespace is listed nowhere.
The root of the tree is listed the way a namespace is listed.
The root's parts are the parts the page type saying what a command is states.
No listing reads the whole roster of commands.
A namespace with no part is answered as a name no command carries.
The whole list of commands is read only where a name was not answered.
A command in that list is written as the call reaching it rather than as its slug.
The name such a refusal points at is written the same way.
Whether the index carries a command at all is answered without loading a page.
An index naming no page type for commands is not an index with no command.
The checks a kind runs and the readings a change of that kind owes are read off its page.
No command is handed a change kind.
A command is stopped where that command runs past the seconds its page allows.

definition: a name from the command line answered by the command that has it
